lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Marie, Ana here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the walking?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is anyone else at home able to cook?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, being so tired makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walking. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I made a big pot of lentils on Sunday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I cook at home 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 8. Maybe 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 8 and not a 5?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Marie, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Ana. Bye!

tags.note: Repeats line 27 suggestion without new response

flags.reason: Participant said 'I don't really see the point' (possible hopelessness or disengagement); coach moved on at line 19 without exploring. Check mood and hopelessness at next contact.
Coach repeated the same meal-prep suggution from line 27 after the participant had only said 'Right', which reads as pushing advice rather than eliciting the participant's own ideas.

score.summary: Ana used good change-talk elicitation and offered autonomy repeatedly, and Marie left with a concrete goal of cooking at home 4 nights and a barrier plan (walking in the hallway if it rains). However, the 'I don't really see the point' comment at line 18 was not explored, and the cooking suggestion was repeated at line 33 without a clear invitation from Marie.
strengths: Line 23: 'You figured that out on your own' affirms Marie's self-awareness and supports autonomy.
Line 12 and line 54: complex reflections capture ambivalence and her wish to make the plan fit real life.
Line 61-65: confidence scaling followed by 'Why an 8 and not a 5?' drew out her own reasons for confidence.
coaching_tips: At line 18, pause on 'I don't really see the point' with an open question such as 'What's making the point feel unclear right now?' before moving on.
Before repeating a suggestion (line 33), ask 'Would you like to hear what else might work?' or invite Marie's own ideas first.
Add a brief summary before closing the call, reflecting her goal, confidence, and barrier plan, and check her feelings about the plan.
